name: opencode

detect.detect_notes: `opencode --version` prints a bare `1.18.29` (live 2026-09-10). The npm global install (package opencode-ai 1.18.29) exposes only script shims on PATH (opencode / opencode.cmd / opencode.ps1, %APPDATA%\npm); Node >= 20.12 refuses to spawn .cmd without shell. opencode.cmd execs %dp0%\node_modules\opencode-ai\bin\opencode.exe directly (shim read 2026-09-10), so npm_exe resolves the REAL native binary (~180MB, verified on disk and spawned 2026-09-10); platform optionalDependencies (opencode-windows-x64 etc.) sit under opencode-ai/node_modules and the bin exe is the resolved entry. There is no package-level JS entry (package.json bin -> ./bin/opencode.exe), hence no npm_entry.

command.mode_args_notes: The `run` subcommand rides inside mode_args (codex-manifest lesson: the security-critical --agent must land AFTER the subcommand; yargs also accepts root-position flags, verified live 2026-09-10). Rendered fresh shape: `opencode [--model M] run --agent <plan|build> [--auto] --format json`, prompt on stdin. Evidence: `opencode run --help` (1.18.29, 2026-09-10): run [message..], --format default|json, -m/--model provider/model, --agent, --auto ('auto-approve permissions that are not explicitly denied (dangerous!)'), -s/--session, -c/--continue, --fork, --dir. read-only = --agent plan (native read-only plan agent: write denied, SHELL read-only — 2026-09-09 eight-agent probe report §1/§3; live P2 2026-09-10: 'Im in plan mode, so I cant create the file yet', exit 0, file absent). workspace-write = --agent build (edit/bash default allow inside cwd; doom_loop/external_directory default ask and have no headless answer channel, so they fail closed). unattended = build + --auto (native approve-all-not-denied tier; live-verified 2026-09-10: `run --agent build --auto` wrote the file, exit 0; P1-P3 contract probes never exercise it). stdin prompt with empty message positionals is the suite-proven shape (adapters/opencode.mjs buildInvocation writes the prompt file to child stdin; re-verified live 2026-09-10).
command.cwd_notes: opencode anchors its PROJECT root from the inherited PWD env var when present, else the process cwd, else a VCS (.git) walk-up — NOT reliably the spawn cwd. Live-verified 2026-09-10 on 1.18.29: with PWD pointing elsewhere, a run whose spawn cwd was a bare temp dir still wrote its deliverable under PWD (relative tool paths resolve against the anchor); `run --dir <cwd>` overrides the anchor and pins writes to the run cwd even with a poisoned PWD. cwd_arg is spliced AFTER mode_args, so the rendered shape keeps the security order: `opencode [--model M] run --agent <plan|build> [--auto] --dir <run cwd> --format json` (--dir is a run-subcommand flag per run --help; yargs also accepts root-position flags, but paidan does not rely on that). env additionally unsets PWD (belt and suspenders).

env._env_notes: NO_COLOR/TERM=dumb are the suite adapter's static pins (adapters/opencode.mjs buildProviderEnv: the provider never spins up an interactive/colored terminal). PWD={unset} strips the inherited shell PWD so it cannot re-anchor the project root (see cwd_notes). {native_default} = paidan never sets the variable; caller-env values pass through. The suite's OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT permission projection (permission.external_directory allow rules for cwd+add_dirs, permission.edit=deny in read-only — adapters/opencode.mjs buildOpenCodePermission) remains unexpressible in paidan v0: read-only enforcement rests on the plan agent alone, and add_dirs is unsupported on this endpoint in v0.

fs.read.via: all agents (incl. read-only plan) read the cwd natively; live runs 2026-09-10 answered from the working directory

fs.write.via: build agent: edit permission defaults allow inside the project dir (live 2026-09-10: `run --agent build --format json` created probe-write.txt exactly, exit 0); plan agent denies writes (read-only)

shell.exec.via: build agent bash permission (default allow; doom_loop stays ask and fails closed headless); plan agent shell is read-only (2026-09-09 probe report §1/§3)

net.fetch.via: opencode has webfetch/web search tools gated by permission keys; per-agent headless behavior not covered by P1-P3 contract probes

interact.ask.via: headless ask has no answer channel; third-party observation says ask auto-rejects (2026-09-09 probe report §1, 'headless 下 ask 疑似自动拒绝'); not live-probed through paidan

permission.presets_notes: Mapping: read-only=`--agent plan`, workspace-write=`--agent build` (default tier), unattended=`--agent build --auto`. The suite additionally injects OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT permission.edit=deny for read-only as a second layer (adapters/opencode.mjs); paidan v0 cannot express computed env, so plan-agent enforcement is the single layer here (live P2-equivalent verified 2026-09-10: file absent, refusal in final text). unattended (--auto) additionally live-verified 2026-09-10 (write completed, exit 0); the P1-P3 probes never exercise it.

denial_evidence.via: plan-agent write refusal is observable in the final text (live 2026-09-10: 'Im in plan mode, so I cant create the file yet', exit 0, file absent); in-band type:error events carry error.data.message (1.18.29 shape; legacy fixtures used part.message — parser reads both). No stderr refusal signature observed on 1.18.29, so detectRefusals is an honest no-op

resume.notes: Session handle = the ses_... sessionID carried on every stdout event (single unique value per stream; drift degrades the parser). `opencode run --session <ses_id>` continues cross-process (run --help 1.18.29); live-verified 2026-09-10: fresh run remembered a codename, second process `--session <ses> --model <m> run --agent build --format json` recalled it with the same sessionID. Sessions are per-project: resume with the same cwd as the source run. --model/--agent may be re-passed on continue (suite adapter always re-passes them; official inheritance semantics unspecified). `--continue` (latest session) is implicit and never used by paidan; --fork exists but is not used (paidan continues in place, same as the suite). Concurrency on one session handle: officially unspecified.

models.notes: Live enumeration via `opencode models` (root help 1.18.29: 'list all available models'; plain `provider/model` lines, verified 2026-09-10: 7 free `opencode/*` Zen models + 28+ `opencode-go/*` models on this machine). connection = provider prefix: `opencode` = 免凭据 Zen free group, `opencode-go` = Go subscription credential (native auth.json — paidan never reads it), BYOK providers appear when natively configured. Selection = config.json defaults.model or the native default; no cross-connection fallback.

parser_notes: `run --format json` emits NDJSON on stdout (live 1.18.29 shape 2026-09-10): step_start / tool_use / step_finish / text / reasoning / error, every event carrying top-level sessionID. text events carry part.text (blank parts skipped, joined with \n = finalText). step_finish carries part.tokens {input, output, reasoning, cache{read, write}} (+part.cost): usage maps to provider ONLY when exactly one step_finish has valid non-negative safe-integer tokens — zero or multiple step_finish events (normal on tool runs; cumulative vs incremental semantics unproven per contracts/opencode-cli.json usage_contract) collapse usage to null with a warning, never fabricated. type:error events are in-band soft errors (warning + refusal evidence; message read from error.data.message on 1.18.29, part.message on legacy shapes). Non-JSON stdout lines, mid-line EOF and multiple distinct sessionIDs degrade the parser; UNKNOWN event types are known-benign drift (contract failure_policy: 'preserve and ignore') — warning only, never degraded. Evidence: adapters/opencode.mjs analyzeNdjson + fixtures/opencode-cli + live 1.18.29 runs 2026-09-10.

effort.notes: `opencode run --help` 1.18.30: `--variant  model variant (provider-specific reasoning effort, e.g., high, max, minimal)`. Values are provider-specific; the option list is exactly the help's examples. Absent = native default. effort × resume combination UNVERIFIED (flag shape verified for fresh runs only; resume carries its own session settings per the endpoint).
